paper_title: Efficient Ensemble for Fine-tuning Language Models on Multiple Datasets
caption: We show the empirical generalization errors (termed Error in the figures) and estimated Hessian traces of the loss for fine-tuned adapters (using QAdapter on Llama-3-8B) across various hidden dimensions. Smaller adapters achieve the lowest generalization errors. Additionally, the Hessian trace values correlate with generalization errors, suggesting that smaller adapters tend to converge to flatter minima.
model_annotation: The plot illustrates the relationship between the rank and errors (RTE) for fine-tuned adapters, showing how the error changes with varying ranks. The x-axis, labeled 'Rank', has a logarithmic scale, spanning from 4 to 256, with tick labels at 4, 16, 64, and 256. The y-axis, labeled 'Errors (RTE)', is on a linear scale, ranging from 0.3 to 0.9, with tick labels at 0.3, 0.6, and 0.9. A single line is plotted, colored black, with green circular markers, and a solid line style, showing a decrease from approximately 0.35 at a rank of 4 to around 0.3 at a rank of 16, followed by an increase to about 0.37 at a rank of 64, and further rising to approximately 0.62 at a rank of 256; error bars are present around each data point, indicating variability in the error measurements.
